name: Paris-Le Bourget Airport

curfew.v: jet take-offs, use of reverse thrust and use of runway 2 by aircraft over 5.7 tonnes are banned between 22:15 and 06:00
curfew.applies_to: jet take-offs, reverse thrust, runway 2 for aircraft over 5.7 t

runway.v: three runways: 07/25, 2,991 m by 45 m (the longest); 03/21, 2,395 m by 45 m; 09/27, 1,847 m by 45 m

ppr.v: VFR flights need prior permission by email at least 48 working hours ahead (helicopters and some public missions exempt)
ppr.quote: PPR requests must be sent by email with at least 48 working HR PN to ppr-vfr-lfpb@aviation-civile.gouv.fr

handling.v: handling by an approved based company is mandatory
handling.quote: Mandatory assistance from approved based societies.

missing: max_aircraft (only in a superseded AIP edition; current edition not read)
notes: French eAIP, Légifrance (arrêté of 15 Feb 2011 on Le Bourget restrictions) and most Paris Aéroport pages (bot protection) could not be opened. The 22:15-06:00 ban is on jet take-offs (not landings), reverse thrust and runway 2 for aircraft over 5.7 t; it is not a full closure. The ADP page's own time base is assumed local; it does not say UTC. COHOR also links an arrêté of 23 June 2023 making Le Bourget coordinated for the 2023 Rugby World Cup; status beyond that event is unclear. COHOR page last modified 9 Jul 2025. | 2026-10-27 run: Current SIA eAIP HTML page (AIRAC 01 OCT 2026) could not be opened; runway, ARP, location and wingspan limit come from AIP France AD 2 LFPB pages (AIRAC AMDT 02/25, 20 FEB 2025) as republished by DIRCAM; operator, customs, PPR and handling from the SIA VAC atlas of the 01 OCT 2026 edition. The PPR rule in the AIP applies to VFR flights; the AIP does not state a PPR for IFR business flights. The VAC also states jets may not leave the stand for take-off from 2115 to 0500 UTC winter time (consistent with the already verified 22:15-06:00 local rule). Facts from the superseded edition other than runway, location and operator were not used (max_aircraft).
